close_reason: Renamed Luau and Odin SDK entry packages to bytorio and standardized the byt namespace throughout examples, templates, generators, tests and docs. Updated editor mirrors, managed aliases, generated entry/assets names and watcher exclusions; preserved user settings, JavaScript console and existing cartridge formats. acceptance_criteria: Fresh projects and examples build through both SDKs, analysis/module resolution uses bytorio, no authored SDK console namespace/import remains, complete validation passes, and the focused migration is committed.

close_reason: Both SDK package identities and byt namespaces are migrated across authored code, project tooling and documentation. Full conformance passed, migration instructions are in sdk/README.md, and cartridge ABI/profile behavior is preserved.

title: Present committed GPU attachments directly
description: Follow compatible-batch residency with successful-commit GPU publication, direct final presentation and lazy logical synchronization. Cover HUD composition, rollback, device failure and attachment allocation/transfer counters. Qualify representative moving racer before/after on both SDKs and native/browser.
close_reason: Direct committed GPU presentation implemented and verified in both SDKs on native/browser; CPU remains default. Full conformance, GPU suites and proxy/riverside benchmarks passed.
notes: Implemented atomic versioned GPU snapshot publication, direct presentation, lazy logical synchronization, opaque HUD composition, rollback and device-loss reporting. Both SDKs/native/browser pass full 25-gate validation and five GPU suites. Model proxy before/after and moving riverside benchmarks pass; see docs/gpu-attachment-measurements.md. Complete eight-kart racer qualification remains in bytorio-10. Reports: build/validation/2026-10-21T15-43-48.181Z-c04aef6c-03a9-47d6-be9f-a4b8042aa94e/report.json and build/validation/2026-10-21T15-53-17.683Z-33859db5-2add-42c8-bd66-ef568d48dce3/report.json. title: Retain compatible GPU attachment batches
description: Keep private color/depth scratch resident across material, camera, clip and load-pass changes within a transaction; synchronize at CPU consumers, attachment switches and publication. Preserve software default and rollback.
close_reason: Implemented compatible GPU color/depth sequences in native and browser players, CPU/publication barriers, rollback/failure coverage and transfer/allocation counters. Both SDK hardware suites and all 25 validation gates passed. Rotating-model comparison halves attachment transfers; results and reproduction are documented in docs/gpu-attachment-measurements.md.
acceptance_criteria: Native and browser GPU fixtures independently verify color/depth, load passes, CPU barriers, offscreen targets, rollback and failure. Transfer counters demonstrate one upload/readback pair per compatible sequence. Both SDK integrations and full validation pass; record focused before/after timings.

title: Prevent repeated support staging on unchanged builds
description: Windows copyFile preserves source modification times. Newly staged dependency files could therefore remain older than the build recipe, causing repeated native/web support staging during otherwise unchanged aggregate builds. The actual-copy regression reproduces this with all declared outputs present.
close_reason: Root cause fixed, real-copy regression preserved invalidation, original repro no longer repeats staging, and the single final full run demonstrated 21.55 percent less wall time with all 24 gates passing.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive unchanged build:odin runs skip all staging and compilation after a relevant task configuration edit. Real copied outputs with old source mtimes have regression coverage. Real asset changes and missing outputs still rebuild affected artifacts; assertions and production flags remain unchanged.
notes: Fixed by dating completed staging outputs; file contents and source modification times are unchanged. Regression failed before the fix (second unchanged run staged twice) and passed afterward, including real source edits, recipe edits, missing outputs and repeated aggregate invocations after configuration edits. Two original unchanged build:odin calls took 2.474s/2.397s; after one repair stage, warm calls took 0.340s/0.338s with no staging or compilation. All 27 copied output hashes matched. Focused lint, formatting, five build-task tests and player-export tests passed. Exactly one final full run passed all 24 gates with stable source: build/validation/2026-10-21T05-40-38.179Z-ed7dac39-32c8-4292-9e11-0c0fa7d3e295/report.json. Full wall time fell from 500.561s to 392.709s, saving 107.852s (21.55 percent). The same 38 build:odin invocations fell from 91.783s to 13.394s; recorded support staging commands fell from 68 to zero. Gate inventory, all five unit-package executions and recorded browser operation counts match the baseline; the new copy regression adds coverage. Single-host before/after samples, including regression overhead. Full comparison and focused measurements: build/support-staging-diagnosis/end-to-end.json, baseline.json and after.json.

title: Record browser phase timings and qualify iteration savings
close_reason: Browser timing journals, summaries, regression checks, documentation and single full-run qualification are complete with all 24 gates passing.
notes: One final full validation passed all 24 gates with stable source: build/validation/2026-10-21T05-22-29.136Z-e767de02-eddd-4b27-aff0-f77bb68352c9/report.json. Browser journals recorded 16 launches, 312 evaluations, 171 waits and screenshots; callbacks, receiver binding, results and error identity have regression coverage. Cache regression: fresh baseline 72.2s, final 36.6s. Recorded Odin unit commands: 31.1s across nine commands previously, 11.7s across five now; each of the five distinct suites executes once. Full wall time was 500.6s versus prior 466.3s, so no end-to-end speedup claim: the same 38 build:odin calls grew from 14.2s to 91.8s due to repeated support staging while compiled artifacts were reused. Comparison retained in build/validation/iteration-savings-summary.json. Follow-up tracks that separate cache behavior; no second full run was started.

title: Deduplicate identical Odin unit checks within validation
close_reason: Identical 3D and audio unit suites execute once per source state within a validation invocation; standalone checks and new invocations execute again. Success receipts retain diagnostics; failures do not create receipts. Focused real suites passed with one 3D and one audio unit execution across five gates; new helper and runner scope tests plus ESLint passed. Evidence: build/validation/2026-10-21T05-15-19.164Z-ed01c047-029d-4083-be2c-b1843924e5fc/report.json and build/validation/2026-10-21T05-19-05.155Z-9bc252f6-5b0f-490c-93fe-6ba9013c004c/report.json.

close_reason: All scheduler invalidation scenarios and duplicate-execution detection preserved. Evidence: build/validation/2026-10-21T05-09-37.857Z-15b2c70a-c906-488e-add8-2e0eb1df037f/report.json and build/validation/2026-10-21T05-12-58.046Z-5d211ecb-15eb-4c9e-b300-5404f4ad58f5/report.json.

title: Integrate build caching and encode efficient iteration guidance
description: Merge the completed build-task split with the billboard changes, preserve all tests and issue records, document normal cache use versus forced rebuilds, and make text checkout endings deterministic.
close_reason: Combined conformance, GPU qualification, cache guidance and deterministic LF checkouts are complete; integrate both histories into main.
acceptance_criteria: Combined full conformance and relevant GPU gates pass with stable source. Main retains both histories. Project guidance gives focused-check, cache recovery and dependency-edit rules without requiring a new skill.
notes: Merged main billboard changes with all 13 issue records preserved. Added cache decisions and LF checkout policy, verified with core.autocrlf=true. Qualification exposed an existing AudioWorklet test startup race: failed PCM aligned exactly after a 512-frame shift. A 50ms setup delay failed the real verifier before the fix. Two consecutive synthesis gates (normal and stress each) plus ordinary audio passed with stable source: build/validation/2026-10-21T04-48-05.179Z-bb8e6e2f-d6ca-4ea3-b626-1a98b7fc7475/report.json. close_reason: Build-task caching, dependency regressions, iteration guidance, unit deduplication, browser timing, and copied-output timestamp handling are complete and verified. No remaining child work.
acceptance_criteria: Independent artifacts rebuild only for relevant inputs or missing outputs. Complete validation and cache invalidation checks pass. Reproducible before/after measurements and limitations are documented.

Final full conformance passed all 24 gates with stable source and unchanged unit/browser coverage. Latest end-to-end wall time is 392.709s versus 500.561s before the staging fix; comparison retained under build/support-staging-diagnosis/.

close_reason: Split native, CPU/GPU/audio Wasm, hello, fixtures and support staging into independently cached tasks. Import-closure, invalidation, missing-output and existing export tests pass. Full player execution and comparative timings are tracked by the qualification child.
acceptance_criteria: Browser support edits stage files without compiling. Each missing output is recovered. Native/browser binaries retain production flags and target-specific dependencies.

title: Accelerate textured meshes and qualify the material API
description: Implement native/browser GPU textured triangles and versioned texture/material residency through the same typed APIs, retain CPU quality rendering, and finish the textured-mesh feature documentation and end-to-end fixtures. Preserve opt-in GPU operation and ordinary colored/surface-sampled scenes.
close_reason: Implemented UV transport and textured rendering in optional software-quality, native OpenGL and browser WebGL paths, resident UV geometry and bounded versioned texture caches. Added accurate source-upload/cache diagnostics and both-SDK motion/edit/display fixtures. All 48 native/browser hardware matrix cases passed: build/validation/2026-10-21T02-59-59.256Z-5b4124f8-8565-49e0-b4f1-ac7e8d10d6ba/report.json. Full 22-gate conformance and legacy GPU/riverside surface gates passed with matching source: build/validation/2026-10-21T03-01-30.372Z-c9075d9e-23a1-4329-93e3-be2638ec998e/report.json and build/validation/2026-10-21T03-10-07.115Z-326a7a29-1806-43c3-be0d-e7ea43b9e954/report.json. GPU acceleration remains opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: Both SDKs render textured perspective meshes on native/browser CPU, streamed GPU and resident GPU paths with supported SSAA modes. Independent expected UV/color/depth tests complement cross-host parity. Stationary and moving draws reuse geometry and texture snapshots until versions change; destruction, palette/texture updates, rollback, device failure and budgets are correct. Full conformance and hardware GPU tests pass, with documented API/profile compatibility and measured transfers.

title: Render textured perspective meshes in the CPU path
description: Extend the typed textured-resource lifecycle with explicit material draws through both SDKs. Implement clipping, perspective-correct UV interpolation, nearest sampling, independent U/V repeat or clamp, vertex tint, lighting/fog, depth and feedback checks. Keep optional GPU execution correct through explicit CPU barriers until the GPU slice is complete.
close_reason: Implemented explicit textured draws in both SDKs with CPU homogeneous clipping, perspective UVs, independent clamp/repeat, tint, lighting, fog and strict depth. Independent sampling and rollback fixtures plus actual native/browser PNG and loose-player checks pass. Mixed GPU/CPU draws flush safely and invalidate stale GPU previews. Full validation passed all 22 gates with matching source: build/validation/2026-10-21T02-35-58.187Z-e8e41cbf-6c59-4da4-9f9d-5a56202c6872/report.json. GPU and quality execution remain in the next acceleration child.
acceptance_criteria: Both SDKs draw and release an equivalent textured perspective scene on native/browser CPU paths. Independent tiny-texture fixtures cover orientation, repeat/clamp, perspective, clipping, tint, fog, depth, resource feedback and rollback. Existing colored rendering remains compatible. Full conformance passes and limitations of the intermediate GPU fallback are documented.

title: Establish textured 3D resource ownership in both SDKs
description: Add a separately negotiated experimental textured-3D profile without changing existing profiles. Implement typed immutable UV meshes and materials referencing existing RGBA textures, with equivalent Luau/Odin constructors and destruction. This slice establishes lifecycle and transport; textured draw execution is the next dependent slice.
close_reason: Implemented separately negotiated SDK 0.4 resource lifecycles, UV mesh ownership, typed materials and pinned RGBA textures in both SDKs. Independent invalid-packet, byte/hash, budget, rollback and reload tests pass on native/browser PNG and loose games. Full validation passed all 22 gates: build/validation/2026-10-21T02-12-53.488Z-dfc57173-9684-4570-b02d-cf285217001d/report.json. Textured draw execution remains in the dependent CPU and GPU slices.
acceptance_criteria: Native/browser loaders validate the exact new profile tuple for PNG and loose cartridges. Both SDKs create and destroy UV meshes/materials through the shared resource protocol. Independent tests verify descriptor bytes, upload ownership, invalid UV/index/texture/sampler data, resource bounds, stale handles, pinned texture lifetime, reset and atomic rollback. Existing stable and compact-3D profiles reject new opcodes and retain current behavior. Complete conformance gates pass.

title: Qualify the 3D racer on native and browser
description: Establish whether the actual console can sustain the refined eight-kart workload at a 60 FPS target. Riverside and the pseudo-3D racing demo are useful baselines but do not establish this workload's budget. Reference: docs/riverside-console-measurements.md and docs/development.md.
design: Choose and record explicit desktop and lower-powered target hardware. Use repeatable motion-heavy replays after builds finish, with serial benchmark runs. Cover both SDKs, native/browser, both display modes, CPU baseline and opt-in GPU/resident paths, and SSAA off/2x/1080p. Verify capped/custom/native/uncapped rendering preserves fixed simulation timing. Separate draw/update timings, readbacks/uploads, presentation and delivered FPS; describe browser scheduling/scanout measurement limits.
acceptance_criteria: Retain raw local reports and publish portable summaries of p50/p95/p99 frame times, delivered FPS, missed frame budgets, startup-to-first-complete-frame, PNG size, guest/runtime/resource/device memory and transfer traffic. Compare CPU/GPU and before/after attachment residency on the same workload without overlapping heavy jobs. Verify gameplay and image correctness before timing, report hardware-specific 60 FPS outcomes and quality fallbacks honestly, and record remaining bottlenecks rather than extrapolating from the independent JS viewer.
notes: Full racer qualification also completes the GPU-residency parent acceptance criteria. Direct committed presentation is implemented and qualified using the rotating imported-model proxy and moving riverside scene; repeat the before/after comparison on the completed eight-kart showcase after baseline/polish work. This issue remains open; the implementation parent does not block its qualification child.

title: Polish the 3D racer with imported assets and effects
description: Integrate the new rendering and asset features into the racing baseline to demonstrate a coherent developer workflow and a more refined visual result. Use original small assets for textured roads, road markings, karts, signs, scenery and effects. References: docs/racing-demo.md and the shared SDK documentation.
design: Retain the eight-kart perspective workload and deterministic core gameplay. Add imported named kart parts, wheel animation, cutout scenery, simple ground shadows, smoke/dust/boost effects and a stable HUD. Package equivalent game content for both SDKs and support the existing display, frame-rate and renderer settings. Keep assets within the current cartridge profile unless indexed loading is demonstrably needed; larger packaging is not an artificial blocker for a small showcase.
acceptance_criteria: Both SDKs produce playable native/browser PNG cartridges with comparable visuals, responsive chase-camera handling, completed race/restart flow and bounded effects. Integration fixtures cover opaque/cutout/transparent ordering, camera clipping, moving karts, HUD placement and resource cleanup. CPU-compatible simpler games remain unaffected, quality options are explicit, and launch/asset-authoring documentation is reproducible without machine-specific paths.

title: Build a true 3D kart-racing baseline in both SDKs
description: Build a small original perspective kart racer against the current colored-mesh APIs so new rendering work has a representative workload. The existing Copper Circuit demo uses pseudo-3D horizontal spans and sprites; its timings do not qualify a general 3D racer. References: docs/racing-demo.md and docs/compact-3d.md.
close_reason: Implemented Sunline Sprint in both SDKs: original elevated perspective course, eight karts, chase camera, drift/launch/turbo mechanics, collisions, checkpoints, three laps, restart and HUD; CPU default and explicit GPU residency. Full 26-gate validation and optional GPU native/browser replay pass at both display modes. Independent handling/elevation assertions and SDK state/image parity pass. Guides and measured startup, memory, cartridge size and stage timings are recorded in docs/kart-racing.md and build/kart3d-benchmarks/e7137de1-c8c8-4497-b461-ead3dde737ec/report.json. Full-course hardware qualification and imported-asset/effects polish remain separate work.
design: Start with colored indexed geometry: a circuit with hills/ramps, a chase camera, a player kart plus seven AI karts, basic steering/acceleration/braking, track contact, simple collision/off-road handling, checkpoints/laps, race restart and a 2D HUD. Use fixed simulation timing and ordinary model transforms for wheels/parts. Implement gameplay in Luau and Odin through the shared player; do not require textures, full rigid-body physics or the orthographic surface-sampling experiment to start.
acceptance_criteria: Both cartridges run standalone native/browser at 320x180 and 640x360 with a genuine perspective camera and depth-tested track/karts. Scripted replays independently verify track progress, collision/off-road behavior, elevation contact, lap completion and restart, alongside SDK parity. Record baseline startup, cartridge size, update/draw timings and memory for CPU and opt-in GPU paths. Provide reproducible mise launch/build commands; do not make unsupported 60 FPS claims.

title: Keep compatible 3D color and depth passes GPU resident
description: Reduce the current GPU-to-CPU color/depth readback and logical-snapshot re-upload costs for a moving racer. Resident meshes already avoid geometry uploads, but attachments still cross the CPU boundary after batches. Reference: docs/compact-3d.md#execution-and-ownership and docs/implementation-plan.md#4g-gpu-execution-and-configurable-presentation.
design: Track attachment ownership and dirty state across compatible passes; synchronize only when an actual CPU composition, readback or other consumer requires it. Present directly from resident attachments when possible. Preserve transaction-private scratch and successful-commit publication, depth continuity, HUD composition, explicit readbacks, cache eviction and device failure behavior. Keep acceleration opt-in and retain the default CPU path.
acceptance_criteria: Native/browser GPU traces prove compatible 3D passes avoid redundant readbacks/uploads and unchanged geometry stays resident. Independent expected-color/depth tests cover clear/load, multiple passes, CPU barriers, offscreen targets, HUD ordering, rollback, stale handles, feedback rejection and device failure. Counters distinguish transferred and allocated bytes. Record before/after representative racer results without removing software conformance or imposing a GPU requirement on simpler games.
notes: Both attachment implementation children are complete: compatible private batches and direct committed presentation with lazy CPU synchronization. Full conformance and five native/browser GPU suites pass for both SDKs; proxy before/after and moving riverside measurements are documented in docs/gpu-attachment-measurements.md. Remaining acceptance work is full eight-kart racer qualification in child bytorio-10 after the showcase is built. No descendant remains active at this verified implementation boundary.

title: Import glTF meshes, textures and named model parts
description: Create a reproducible artist-friendly path from a small glTF/GLB asset into shared cartridge assets usable by both SDKs. Cover track meshes, textured kart bodies, wheels and named parts so game authors do not hand-author vertex tables. References: tools/sdk/project.mjs, sdk/README.md and docs/compact-3d.md.
close_reason: Implemented bounded static glTF/GLB import, PNG base-color and cutout conversion, named rigid hierarchies and shared mesh instances, readable Luau/Odin modules, safe generated-directory publication, CLI integration and authoring examples. Existing ABI and default CPU requirements are unchanged. All 41 importer checks and 24 native/browser CPU integration cases passed inside full 25-gate validation: build/validation/2026-10-21T06-29-11.659Z-4f640a2d-de6b-45e5-85b2-c85dbed778c6/report.json. All 48 native/browser GPU cases passed with matching final source: build/validation/2026-10-21T06-39-19.957Z-12f7b593-58d2-421a-8f7b-ca0422de2ffd/report.json. Both SDK 0.4 opaque and SDK 0.5 masked exports were verified. Usage, budgets and rendering reductions are documented in docs/model-import.md.
design: Use the existing mise/JavaScript tool workflow. Define a small supported glTF subset for static indexed triangle meshes, UVs, vertex colors, textures, transforms and named nodes. Emit validated runtime assets with stable names and size reports. Convert coordinate, winding and color conventions explicitly. Permit rigid part animation in game code; skeletal animation, morph targets and broad extension support remain deferred.
acceptance_criteria: One checked fixture imports reproducibly and loads through Luau and Odin on native/browser. Tests use independent expected coordinates, hierarchy transforms, UVs, colors and resource sizes, including malformed accessors, external paths and oversized images. Unsupported features produce clear diagnostics without corrupting a previous build. SDK starter/examples document importing and animating wheels/rigid parts with existing tools.

title: Add depth-tested billboards and alpha-cutout materials
description: Provide textured 3D billboards and alpha cutout for trees, fences, item icons and simple shadow artwork in a moving perspective scene. These must participate in scene depth rather than being ordinary HUD sprites. Reference: docs/compact-3d.md and sdk/api.md.
close_reason: Implemented the SDK 0.5 alpha preview, upright/camera-facing billboards, explicit cutout thresholds, rejected-fragment depth holes, shared examples and shadow recipe. Kept GPU optional and older Luau bundles within 256 KiB through profile-gated helpers and generated capability metadata. Full 23-gate validation passed with matching source: build/validation/2026-10-21T03-59-34.700Z-c2c84bf5-b292-420e-ac84-d692879e411e/report.json. All four hardware gates passed with matching source: build/validation/2026-10-21T04-08-35.273Z-9609c390-0621-4ba6-b2f1-44b8fa540263/report.json. Independent cutoff/depth probes remain exact; bounded cross-driver perspective differences retain captures.
design: Build on typed textured materials. Define camera-facing and upright billboards, explicit size/pivot/orientation and alpha threshold. A rejected texel must not write color or depth. Offer a documented simple kart-shadow recipe without adding shadow maps. Keep transformations and depth semantics equivalent on CPU/GPU and through both SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Native/browser examples through Luau and Odin show billboards correctly occluded by tracks and karts, upright vegetation under camera orbit, transparent cutout holes and a simple kart shadow. Independent fixtures check pivots, cutoff boundaries, clipping, depth writes and texture sampling. Existing opaque and HUD rendering remains compatible, and all allocations/commands obey published budgets.

title: Add textured meshes and typed materials to both SDKs
description: The current 3D vertex has position and opaque color only. Add UVs and typed material/texture bindings for perspective tracks, road markings, signs and kart artwork, using equivalent Luau and Odin authoring APIs and native/browser CPU/GPU implementations. Reference: docs/compact-3d.md#sdk-surface and #rendering-semantics.
close_reason: Completed the resource-lifecycle, CPU draw and optional GPU acceleration children. Both SDKs expose typed immutable UV meshes, pinned RGBA materials and explicit material draws through the separately negotiated experimental SDK 0.4 profile. Native/browser CPU, quality, streamed GPU and resident GPU paths are independently checked, with complete conformance and existing GPU/surface compatibility gates passing. API, wire layout, ownership, limits, cache counters and execution choices are documented. Alpha cutout, billboards, transparent effects and removal of attachment transfers remain separate planned features.
design: Start with one small texture/material/mesh lifecycle through both SDKs, then add perspective-correct UV interpolation, nearest filtering, wrapping/clamping and vertex tint. Generate protocol values from the existing schema. Specify texture ownership, sampler state, target feedback hazards, destruction, budget charging and version/profile negotiation. Preserve old colored meshes and stable profile behavior; custom shaders and advanced material graphs are outside this slice.
acceptance_criteria: Both SDKs create, bind, draw and destroy a textured perspective mesh on native/browser CPU and GPU paths. Independent tiny-texture fixtures verify UV orientation, perspective interpolation, tint, wrapping/clamping, clipping and depth. Invalid handles, UVs, formats, bounds, feedback and over-budget packets reject atomically. Resident geometry and texture snapshots are reused until their versions change. Existing cartridges, CPU defaults and full conformance gates remain valid.
notes: Resource lifecycle and CPU textured drawing children are complete and fully verified. Between implementation commits; next is GPU and software-quality texture execution, residency and material qualification.

title: Deliver a refined 3D kart-racing showcase
description: Extend the existing compact 3D foundation into a developer-ready path for an original textured kart racer, using the same Luau and Odin SDK contracts on standalone native and browser players. Current meshes, perspective cameras, depth, flat lighting, fog and opt-in GPU residency are a foundation; the existing racing demo is pseudo-3D, and the riverside surface-sampling experiment is orthographic only. References: docs/compact-3d.md, docs/racing-demo.md, docs/implementation-plan.md, docs/riverside-console-measurements.md.
design: Use ordinary textured triangle meshes for a chase-camera racer. Preserve CPU as the default for simpler games and keep GPU acceleration, residency and SSAA opt-in. Establish typed resource ownership, bounds, rollback, compatibility and one lifecycle through both SDKs before expanding features. Defer custom shaders, advanced shadows, skeletal animation, multiplayer and a full physics engine.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible original racing showcase has a true perspective track with elevation, eight moving karts, textured scenery, HUD and bounded visual effects through both SDKs on native and browser. Renderer, asset tooling and packaging changes preserve existing cartridges and CPU-only simple games. All child issues are complete, with independent rendering/behavior fixtures and documented startup, memory, uploads, frame-time and delivered-FPS measurements against a 60 FPS target on identified hardware; distinguish measured results from unsupported guarantees.
notes: Completed the true perspective eight-kart baseline in both SDKs in addition to textured meshes/materials, billboards/cutout, model import and GPU attachment presentation. Full 26-gate validation and optional GPU replay pass on native/browser at both display modes. CPU remains default. See docs/kart-racing.md for controls, implementation limits and local rollout measurements. Imported-asset/effects polish and full-course hardware qualification remain open. No descendant remains active at this verified boundary.

title: Extend PNG cartridges with bounded indexed asset loading
description: The current 2 MiB PNG container ceiling is unsuitable for substantial textured games. Implement a versioned larger-cartridge and asset-loading path toward the project's approximately 128 MiB typical and 512 MiB upper goals. Those are distribution goals, not permission to inflate guest heaps or resident budgets. References: docs/png-cartridges.md and milestone 5 in docs/implementation-plan.md.
design: Define an indexed payload with independently readable entries, explicit encoded/decoded budgets and native/browser capability negotiation. Stream bounded asset chunks from original PNG bytes without decoding the entire cover or loading the whole ROM into linear memory. Account for large textures, geometry and audio separately. Preserve existing PNG/loose cartridges and save identities; do not solve this by raising every runtime limit.
acceptance_criteria: Old cartridges still load, and larger indexed fixtures including near-goal synthetic payloads round-trip on native/browser with bounded startup/working memory. Both SDKs can request, consume and release chunks with clear failure/backpressure semantics. Verify malformed indexes, hashes/CRCs, range bounds, decompression limits, truncated/offline delivery, unsupported profiles and resource rollback. Document exact implemented ceilings and measure cartridge bytes, first frame and peak memory independently.

title: Add transparent 3D effects and bounded particle helpers
description: Support smoke, dust, boost trails and sparks in scene space. Existing 3D rendering requires an opaque pipeline; add explicit blending and depth controls rather than approximating these effects with screen overlays. Reference: docs/compact-3d.md#rendering-semantics.
design: Specify premultiplied-alpha and additive materials, depth testing versus depth writing, and opaque/cutout/transparent ordering with a documented sorting responsibility. Include a bounded reusable sprite-particle example/helper for both languages. Do not add order-independent transparency, volumetrics or a general VFX editor.
acceptance_criteria: Both SDKs render depth-occluded dust/smoke and additive sparks through native/browser CPU/GPU paths. Independent overlap fixtures check blending, sorting, depth-write controls, SSAA resolves and mixed 2D/3D passes. Particle counts, storage and update work remain bounded, repeated effects release resources, and transparent passes preserve transaction rollback and old opaque output.
